sources.note: Brief phonology note only (sec. 1.1): 'Like many African languages, Vata and Gbadi are tone languages. Four lexical tones can be distinguished' (high, mid-high, mid, low); contour tones as sequences of level tones. No statement on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Dida language' (phonology section based on Miller 2005 and Masson 1992), read 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; tone only ('Dida uses tone grammatically'; Abou Dida three level tones).

sources.citation: Vogler, Pierre. 1987 [2e éd. revue et corrigée 2023]. Le parler vata (Côte d'Ivoire). Strasbourg: Université des Sciences Humaines de Strasbourg (Travaux de l'Institut d'Ethnologie de Strasbourg 3). HAL hal-04199475v4, 301 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Phonologie (pp. 10-42) treats consonants, vowels (+/-ATR, nasal, long, asyllabic), tones (ch. IV: four level registers haut / moyen-haut / moyen-bas / bas plus contour 'modulés', 'Register tone language with contour overlap'), distribution, and 'Démarcation' (ch. VI: boundaries signalled by vowel harmony and tone distribution, a glottal-stop juncture) — no word accent/stress is posited or discussed; 'intensité'/'allongement' appear only for expressive ideophone lengthening and sentence-level key changes.

sources.citation: Charette, Monik. 1984. Analyse phonologique des emprunts en dida de Niakassé. Revue québécoise de linguistique 14(1): 87-111. doi:10.7202/602529ar
sources.note: Different variety (Niakassé/Yocoboué Dida = yoco1235). Says Dida is a tone language with three phonetic tones, contrasted with French/English 'langues à accent'; the accent of loanwords is rendered by a Haut-Bas tone sequence on the source-stressed syllable. No statement about native word stress.

sources.citation: Kaye, Jonathan D. & Monik Charette. 1981. Tone sensitive rules in Dida. In W. R. Leben (ed.), Précis from the 12th Conference on African Linguistics, Studies in African Linguistics Supplement 8, 82-85.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Data from 'the Dida dialect spoken at the village of Srikpalilie near the town of Lakota'; ten vowels (5 x ATR), 'Dida has four lexically distinct level tones.. Contour tones are analyzed and transcribed as sequences of level tones'; paper is about segmental rules conditioned by tone.

sources.citation: Kaye, Jonathan D. 1981. La sélection des formes pronominales en vata. Revue québécoise de linguistique 11(1). doi:10.7202/602483ar
sources.note: Nothing; morphology of pronoun selection; mentions the four tones in passing.

sources.citation: Kaye, Jonathan D. 1981. Les diphtongues cachées du vata. Studies in African Linguistics 12(3): 225-244.
sources.note: Nothing; presents the Vata ten-vowel ATR system and hidden diphthongs; no mention of accent/stress.
